issues.display_title: Issue #129: Scrollbar on Preview Page is Too Thin and Hard to Grab
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Image Issue

Problem

The scrollbar on the Preview page is too thin to see and almost impossible to grab. The
track is 4px wide (2px tall for horizontal), so catching the thumb needs pixel-perfect
mouse precision and the scroll position is hard to read at a glance.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder with more images than fit on screen
  2. Look at the scrollbar on the right of the browse grid
  3. Try to click and drag the thumb

The bar is barely visible and the cursor slips off the thumb.

Expected

The scrollbar is thick enough to see and to click/hold/drag without precise aiming,
closer to a standard application scrollbar, and stays consistent in light and dark mode.

Note

The scrollbar is styled globally, not per page — src/renderer/index.css sets
::-webkit-scrollbar for the whole app, so this affects every scrollable area, not just
Preview.

Fix in progress on feat/renderer-refactor-g0:

  • src/renderer/index.css — ::-webkit-scrollbar width 4px -> 8px, height 2px -> 6px

Thumb/track colours and radius are unchanged; the hidden-scrollbar cases
(scrollbar-width: none utility, .rename-input) stay hidden as before.

QA Testing Summary — 2026-09-01

Verdict: PASSED. User-confirmed real-device validation completed successfully.

Test execution

ID Method Scenario Expected Result
TC-01 Black-box Preview folder with an overflowing image grid Vertical scrollbar is visible and can be dragged reliably Pass
TC-02 Black-box Drag the Preview scrollbar thumb repeatedly Scroll position changes without cursor slip or pixel-perfect aiming Pass
TC-03 Black-box Dark Mode Preview scrollbar Readable track/thumb and reliable drag behavior Pass
TC-04 Black-box Light Mode Preview scrollbar Readable track/thumb and reliable drag behavior Pass
TC-05 Gray-box Global scrollbar regression scope Preview behavior is corrected without changing intentionally hidden controls Pass

Confusion matrix

Observed state Expected accessible scrollbar Expected hidden scrollbar
Preview scrollable grid True positive: visible, easy-to-grab scrollbar Not applicable
.rename-input exception Not applicable True positive: remains intentionally hidden

Code review

Method Evidence Result
White-box src/renderer/index.css defines global ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px; height: 6px; }. Pass
White-box Light/Dark track, thumb, hover, and active styles remain defined; .rename-input retains its explicit hidden-scrollbar rule. Pass
Gray-box Global stylesheet affects Preview and other scrollable renderer surfaces consistently. Pass
Black-box Tester validated dragging and visibility in Light and Dark Mode on a real desktop device. Pass

Evidence

The runtime result is user-confirmed. No screenshot/video URL was supplied to QA for publication.

Final status

The Preview scrollbar is visible and usable at the corrected size, works in both themes, and preserves the documented hidden-scrollbar exception.

issues.display_title: Issue #102: Optimize Auto Level: adding files to the queue is slow
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Edit → Auto Level: selecting files and adding them to the queue takes noticeably long before anything shows up in the list, especially for large panoramas.

Root cause: adding to the queue isn't just listing files — useAutoLevel.tsx's processFilesToAdd calls ipc.getPanoLevelMetadata per file (useAutoLevel.tsx:130), which runs full horizon/vanishing-point detection (pano_level::estimate_metadata) synchronously, and Promise.all (useAutoLevel.tsx:149) holds the whole batch back from appearing until every file finishes.

That detection call was paying for more decode work than it needs, in src-tauri/src/pano_level/mod.rs / image_io.rs:

  1. read_rgb always did a full-resolution decode, even though line detection only ever looks at a 1024px-wide analysis image (detect::make_analysis_image downsamples right after).
  2. The equirectangular-ratio guard ran after that full decode, so a clearly-non-panorama file still paid for the full decode before being rejected.

How to reproduce

  1. Open Edit → Auto Level
  2. Select several images (especially large/high-res ones) and add them to the queue
  3. Notice the delay before items appear in the queue list

Fix

Fixed in the working tree (not yet committed):

  • Check the equirectangular ratio from the file header (imagesize::size, no decode) before decoding anything — a non-pano file is rejected instantly.
  • Added image_io::read_rgb_scaled, reusing the same reduced-DCT-scale JPEG decode already used for grid thumbnails (commands::image::decode_jpeg_scaled, made pub(crate)). The dry-run path (estimate_metadata, used for the add-to-queue preview) now decodes at analysis resolution instead of full resolution — up to ~64x less decode work on a large panorama. The real leveling run (level_panorama) still decodes full-res, since it needs to write the corrected output.

cargo check clean, all 20 pano_level unit tests pass.

Goal

Adding files to the Auto Level queue should feel roughly as fast as the other Edit subfeatures (Crop, Enfuse, Resize) — proportional to file count, not to how large each source image is.

Test plan reference

docs/refactor/pre-merge-test-plan.md §4.5, row E-6 Auto Level.

issues.display_title: Issue #67: Fix Issue "Preview" Button Loads Incorrect Folder Context from Inside Editing Tools
issues.main_description_html:
A critical context loss bug has been reported. When a user is working inside an editing tool (such as "Auto Level") within a specific folder, and they click the "Preview" button in the top navigation bar, the application routes them to the Preview screen but fails to maintain the current folder's context.

Instead of previewing the images from the folder they were just working in, the system loads a Preview state from an entirely different, previously accessed folder.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "There is a bug, let's say I am in a tool like Auto Level, and I click Preview, it takes me back to Preview from another folder, not the current folder."

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When a user is inside an editing tool (e.g., Auto Level) for Folder A, clicking "Preview" successfully opens the Preview screen populated with the images from Folder A.
  2. The application never loads images from Folder B (a previous session) when transitioning to Preview from Folder A.

🧪 Testing Scenario (for QA)

Feature: "Preview" button navigation from inside an editing tool
Goal: Verify Preview always shows the CURRENT folder's images, never a previously opened folder.

Pre-conditions

  • App running (v1.1.4+); at least two different folders with images available (call them Folder A and Folder B).

Test 1 — Core repro (current folder context preserved)

  1. Open Folder B, go to Preview at least once (to seed a previous Preview state), then leave.
  2. Open Folder A.
  3. Enter an editing tool for Folder A, e.g. Edit → Auto Level.
  4. While inside Auto Level, click Preview in the top nav.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview opens populated with Folder A images (the folder currently being worked on).
  • ❌ Fail: Preview shows Folder B images (stale/previous-session context).

Test 2 — Multiple tools

  • Repeat Test 1 using other tools (e.g. Image Minifier, AI Nadir Patching) to confirm the fix is not tool-specific.

Test 3 — Multiple folder switches

  1. Open Folder A → Preview → back.
  2. Open Folder B → enter a tool → click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder B (the latest/current folder), not Folder A.

Test 4 — Fresh session / single folder

  1. Open only Folder A (no prior Preview history), enter a tool, click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder A correctly (no empty/incorrect state).

Regression checks

  • Preview opened directly from File Manager still shows the correct current folder.
  • Image count and file details panel in Preview match Folder A's contents.
  • Navigating tool → Preview → back to tool keeps Folder A context intact.

DEMO BY DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-17.at.15.58.56.mov

QA Sanity Testing Summary — 2026-09-01

Verdict: FAILED — confirmed coding regression.

The requested Folder A/Folder B Preview-context scenarios were manually validated on a real desktop device and passed. However, switching from Preview to Edit causes the authenticated app to show six or more duplicate error toasts: Could not load your profile. Please try again later. This is a visible navigation regression and not an expected validation message.

User-confirmed runtime evidence

  • Tester-confirmed execution: all requested Folder A/Folder B scenarios completed successfully.
  • Reproduction: Preview → tap Edit.
  • Actual: six or more duplicate profile-load error toasts appear.
  • Evidence timestamp: approximately 00:55.
2026-09-01.10-47-35.mp4

Test execution

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-01 Black-box Folder B Preview → Folder A → Auto Level → Preview Folder A remains active Folder A context was retained Pass
TC-02 Black-box Repeat the context transition through a second Edit tool Current folder remains active Current folder was retained Pass
TC-03 Black-box Multiple Folder A/B switches Latest folder wins; no stale context Latest folder was retained Pass
TC-04 Black-box regression Preview → tap Edit One clean navigation with no profile error toast Six or more Could not load your profile toasts Fail
TC-05 Gray-box Compare observed toast with renderer error path Error should be emitted only for a genuine, handled profile request failure The exact localized error toast is emitted repeatedly Fail

Confusion matrix

Actual runtime state Expected clean navigation Expected error feedback
Normal Preview → Edit navigation True negative: no profile error toast Not expected
Reproduced Preview → Edit navigation False positive: six or more profile error toasts Error feedback was incorrectly surfaced repeatedly

Code review

Review method Evidence Assessment
White-box src/renderer/features/auth/UserDetail.tsx calls GET /users/detail and emits t_user_detail.t_load_profile_failed for every non-401 rejection. This is the exact text seen in the user-confirmed recording. The error path has no visible deduplication or single-flight guard.
Gray-box The shared Header mounts UserDetail; Preview → Edit changes renderer state while preserving the signed-in session. Repeated toasts during that navigation indicate repeated failed profile-load handling rather than a single user action.
Black-box Real-device recording at ~00:55. Reproducible user-facing regression: a single Edit tap produces six or more alerts.

Developer action requested

Investigate why the authenticated profile request/error handler is invoked repeatedly when switching Preview → Edit. Ensure the navigation either reuses valid cached profile data or performs at most one controlled profile refresh, and surface at most one actionable error for a genuine failure. Preserve the now-passing folder-context behavior.
